ochre.displayName: Ochre Ink, the accent token (light theme)

display.purpose: The name in the header; the only h1, which fades in letter by letter on first load. Bricolage 600, 2.75rem → 3rem at sm.

headline.purpose: Section h2s, plain ink. Bricolage 600, 1.5rem → 1.875rem at lg.

title.purpose: Featured project titles. Bricolage 600, 1.25rem → 1.375rem at sm. (Contact email: Bricolage 600, 1.375rem → 1.875rem at sm.)

body.purpose: Intro and project prose in Geist, capped at 36–62ch.

body-sm.purpose: Bullets, result labels, secondary prose, button labels.

label.purpose: Dates, meta lines, footer; tabular-nums in columns.

shadows.name: overlay-control
shadows.purpose: Carousel arrows floating over an image.

motion.name: ease-expo-out
motion.purpose: The house curve: entrance, row expansion, thumbnail scale, copy morph, dialogs.

motion.name: enter-stagger
motion.value: 700ms ease-expo-out; from opacity 0, blur(6px), translateY(6px); 50ms stagger capped at 350ms
motion.purpose: First-load resolve of the header's children; once only.

motion.name: enter-late
motion.purpose: About section entrance after the header.

motion.name: name-letters
motion.value: fade-in 250ms ease per letter; delay calc(var(--i) * 28ms + 80ms); `.letter` spans with --i set per index
motion.purpose: The h1 types itself in on first load; the header resolves in its 50ms stagger around it.

motion.name: color-transition
motion.purpose: Buttons, links and icon buttons on hover.

motion.name: button-press
motion.purpose: Every button and the copy-email button.

motion.name: focus-rows
motion.purpose: Hovering a project row quiets the others; hover-capable devices only.

motion.name: row-expand
motion.value: 300ms ease-expo-out; grid-template-rows 0fr → 1fr; content opacity + blur 300ms with 100ms delay
motion.purpose: Project row disclosure. Every row starts collapsed; following #client-work (or arriving with it in the URL) opens the first client project.

motion.name: scroll-map-tracker
motion.value: left 120ms linear, driven by --progress (0–1) written once per animation frame
motion.purpose: The outlined tracker riding the 28-tick ruler in the desktop scroll minimap; never through React state.

motion.name: scroll-map-label
motion.value: fade-in 250ms ease on each change; left/transform 120ms linear
motion.purpose: The current section label follows the tracker, clamped to the ruler ends, and fades in afresh when the section changes.

motion.name: copy-morph
motion.purpose: Copy icon cross-fades to a check for two seconds.

motion.name: dialog-in
motion.purpose: Lightbox and résumé dialog entrance; backdrop fades 220ms ease-out.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion collapses every transition and animation.

themes.mechanism: Light tokens in @theme; dark overrides under prefers-color-scheme: dark (unless data-theme='light') and under :root[data-theme='dark']. The header toggle sets data-theme and localStorage 'theme'; an inline script in index.html re-applies it before first paint.

narrative.overview:
The well-kept developer portfolio, with its yellow back. v3 began as the category standard at full finish; the user found it too plain, so this pass keeps v3's spacing, pinned layout and row grammar and brings back v2's character: the v2 yellow (`#ffe45b`), bolder surfaces, a display face for headings. Warmth is borrowed from joshwcomeau.com but turned well down, and the interaction finish comes from rauno.me: small, quick, physical CSS responses rather than spectacle. Everything still serves a recruiter on a phone deciding in ten seconds: identity and both actions (email, résumé) on the first screen, then shipped systems with their numbers.

Desktop is two columns: identity pinned on the left, the work scrolling on the right; below `lg` it is one column, identity first. Warm off-white or warm charcoal carry the page in two themes. Yellow does two jobs, each with its own token: a fill for the one primary action and the Contact card, and (as deep ochre in light mode) text for links and focus. Headings are plain ink in Bricolage; the highlighter swipe was tried and removed at the user's request. Structure is still hairline rows and a date column, not cards; the Contact card is the single deliberate exception.

Motion is CSS only, with no animation library: a once-only resolve on first load with the name fading in letter by letter, a rauno.me-style scroll minimap in the desktop nav, rows that quiet their siblings on hover, buttons that press, and an email-copy morph. Reduced motion collapses all of it.
keyCharacteristics: Light and dark themes, following the OS, with a header toggle persisted in localStorage and applied before first paint.
One yellow family split into two roles: fill (`highlight`) and text (`accent`, ochre in light).
Two self-hosted faces: Bricolage Grotesque SemiBold for display, Geist variable for everything else.
Hairline-divided rows and a fixed date column; one full-colour card closes the page.
Flat: depth only on overlays that genuinely float.
CSS-only micro-interactions; ~74 kB gzip JS total.

rules.name: The Two-Yellows Rule
rules.body: Yellow as fill is `highlight`, yellow as text is `accent`. No yellow behind text: the highlighter swipe was removed. Never put `highlight` itself on text against the light canvas; use `accent`, which is ochre there.

rules.name: The One-Yellow-Surface Rule
rules.body: The Contact card is the only full yellow surface; the primary button is the only other yellow fill. Don't tint another section, card or "featured" item yellow.

rules.name: The Two-Border Rule
rules.body: A border is either a hairline (decoration, `border`) or a control edge (`control`, ≥3:1). On a yellow fill the control edge is ink at 60% (4.25:1).

rules.name: The One-Token-Two-Values Rule
rules.body: New colours are added as a light value in `@theme` and a dark override in both dark blocks (OS-preference and `data-theme='dark'`). No component-level hex, no stock Tailwind palette; the dialog scrims (`black/60`, `black/80`) are the only exception.

rules.name: The Display-Is-Rare Rule
rules.body: Bricolage sets only the h1, section h2s, featured project titles and the Contact email. Everything else, including buttons, nav and sub-headings, is Geist. A third family needs the user's sign-off.

rules.name: The Negative-Tracking-Scales-With-Size Rule
rules.body: Tracking tightens only as size grows: -0.025em on the name, -0.02em on the email, -0.015em on h2s and project titles, zero for body and labels.

rules.name: The Pinned-Identity Rule
rules.body: On desktop the name, both actions and the nav never leave view; on mobile they are the first screen. New sections go in the right column, never into the header.

rules.name: The Same-Row Rule
rules.body: Any dated list uses the date-column row (`9.5rem` + content). Don't invent a new list shape for a new kind of entry.

rules.name: The Floats-Only Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this is above the page". Cards, rows, chips and buttons at rest carry none, including the Contact card.

dos: Do define every colour as a token with a light value and a dark override; check both themes for contrast (body ≥4.5:1, control edges ≥3:1) on the composited background, including on the yellow card.
Do use `accent` for yellow text and `highlight` for yellow fills; text on a yellow fill is `on-highlight` (ink).
Do switch focus rings to ink inside any yellow surface.
Do keep touch targets at 2.75rem (44px) below `lg` and 2.5rem (40px) from `lg`.
Do separate content with 1px hairlines and the date-column row; signal importance with order, size or a label.
Do put new motion in CSS on opacity, transform, filter or colour, gate hover effects to hover-capable devices, and make sure the `prefers-reduced-motion` reset covers it.
Do lead project results with the number, in tabular figures.
donts: Don't add a JS animation library or JS-driven animation; all motion is CSS by decision.
Don't add per-section scroll reveals; the entrance runs once, on the header and About only.
Don't set body copy, buttons or nav in Bricolage, or add a third web font.
Don't add a second yellow surface or give one item a tinted "featured" fill; the Contact card is the only one.
Don't put `#ffe45b` text on the light canvas, or use yellow for "running" status; that is `live` green.
Don't wrap content in shadowed cards, or use the hairline token as a control border.
Don't hardcode hex values or Tailwind's stock palette in components (dialog scrims excepted).
